papers.title_in_file: Compare Amazon Braket simulators - Amazon Braket
papers.version_note: Web documentation page text; no page breaks in the text layer, read as one page.
papers.what_it_is: An Amazon Braket Developer Guide page that compares the SV1 and DM1 on-demand simulators with local simulators and gives qubit-count guidance.

assertions.value: The documentation states that on-demand simulators run in the AWS cloud and are designed to scale beyond typical local environments, are optimized for larger circuits, and add some latency overhead per quantum task or batch of quantum tasks.
assertions.anchor: Choosing between local simulators and on-demand simulators (SV1, DM1), p.1
quotes: On-demand simulators run in the AWS cloud and are designed to scale beyond typical local environments.
On-demand simulators are optimized for larger circuits, but add some latency overhead per quantum task or batch of quantum tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own product.

assertions.value: The documentation advises: fewer than 18 qubits, use a local simulator; 18 to 24 qubits, choose a simulator based on the workload; more than 24 qubits, use an on-demand simulator.
assertions.anchor: Choosing between local simulators and on-demand simulators, p.1
quotes: When employing fewer than 18 qubits, use a local simulator.
When employing 18–24 qubits, choose a simulator based on the workload.
When employing more than 24 qubits, use an on-demand simulator.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own product.

assertions.value: For noise simulations the documentation advises: fewer than 9 qubits, use a local simulator; 9 to 12 qubits, choose a simulator based on the workload; more than 12 qubits, use DM1.
assertions.anchor: Choosing between local simulators and on-demand simulators, p.1
quotes: When employing fewer than 9 qubits, use a local simulator.
When employing 9–12 qubits, choose a simulator based on the workload.
When employing more than 12 qubits, use DM1.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own product.

assertions.value: The documentation describes SV1 as a universal state vector simulator that stores the full wave function of the quantum state, applies gate operations to the state sequentially, and stores all possibilities, even the extremely unlikely ones.
assertions.anchor: What is a state vector simulator?, p.1
quotes: SV1 is a universal state vector simulator.
It stores the full wave function of the quantum state and sequentially applies gate operations to the state.
It stores all possibilities, even the extremely unlikely ones.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own product.

assertions.value: The documentation states that SV1 run time for a quantum task increases linearly with the number of gates in the circuit, and that the time required does not depend on the number of shots.
assertions.anchor: What is a state vector simulator?; Types of problems best suited for each simulator, p.1
quotes: The SV1 simulator's run time for a quantum task increases linearly with the number of gates in the circuit.
Generally, the time required grows linearly with the number of gates, while it does not depend on the number of shots.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own product.

assertions.value: The documentation states that SV1 simulates all possibilities and cannot determine which outcomes are likely, so a 30-qubit evaluation must calculate 2^30 configurations, that the limit of 34 qubits is a practical constraint due to memory and storage limitations, and that each added qubit makes the problem twice as hard.
assertions.anchor: Types of problems best suited for each simulator, p.1
quotes: Thus, for a 30-qubit evaluation, SV1 must calculate 2^30 configurations.
The limit of 34 qubits for the Amazon Braket SV1 simulator is a practical constraint due to memory and storage limitations.
Each time you add a qubit to SV1, the problem becomes twice as hard.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own product.

assertions.value: The documentation describes DM1 as simulating quantum circuits with noise: it stores the full density matrix of the system, applies the gates and noise operations of the circuit sequentially, and the final density matrix holds complete information about the quantum state after the circuit runs.
assertions.anchor: What is a density matrix simulator?, p.1
quotes: DM1 simulates quantum circuits with noise.
It stores the full density matrix of the system and sequentially applies the gates and noise operations of the circuit.
The final density matrix contains complete information about the quantum state after the circuit runs.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own product.

assertions.value: The documentation states that DM1 runtime scales linearly with the number of operations but exponentially with the number of qubits, limiting DM1 to circuits of up to 17 qubits.
assertions.anchor: What is a density matrix simulator?; Types of problems best suited for each simulator, p.1
quotes: The runtime scales linearly with the number of operations but exponentially with the number of qubits, limiting DM1 to circuits of up to 17 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own product.

assertions.value: The documentation states that DM1 is best suited for simulating circuits with noise, to be used when the effects of noise on a circuit must be studied or when an algorithm requires density matrix operations.
assertions.anchor: Types of problems best suited for each simulator, p.1
quotes: DM1 is best suited for simulating circuits with noise.
Use DM1 when you need to study the effects of noise on your circuit or when your algorithm requires density matrix operations.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own product.

assertions.value: The documentation states that all Braket simulators can run multiple circuits concurrently, and that concurrency limits vary by simulator and region.
quotes: All Braket simulators give you the ability to run multiple circuits concurrently.
Concurrency limits vary by simulator and region.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describes its own product.
